items.title: A Sydney mother died after drinking 67 cups of water under 24-hour watch
items.description: When Tammy Shipley felt herself sliding into psychosis, she made a heartbreaking decision: She walked into a police station and asked to be arrested, believing prison would keep her safe.

items.title: Anthony Albanese has shown he understands the Westminster system
items.description: This week the Coalition's weakness in Question Time reminded onlookers of Albanese's command of the Westminster system, while Labor insiders expressed their anxieties about One Nation's polling surge.

items.title: Buyer's agency Dashdot collapse leaves hundreds of clients out of pocket
items.description: Liquidators say at least 700 Dashdot clients could be caught up in the buyer's agency collapse, with some who paid large up-front fees fearing they may not get their money back.

items.title: Fastest-rising women's cancer in Australia still has a low profile
items.description: The incidence of the cancer has doubled over the past 25 years. But it's also a disease without a public profile, which means many women aren't aware of the warning signs or the risk factors.

items.title: Trump battleship plan poses new risk to AUKUS, committee fears
items.description: A committee of Congress wants the US Navy to explain how building "Trump-class" battleships will not delay other nuclear-powered boats, such as submarines needed for AUKUS.

items.title: The US ally getting nuclear-powered submarines with no AUKUS deal
items.description: South Korea is taking a different path to Australia in building nuclear-powered submarines, but its plan still hinges on the United States.

items.title: The fake police scam stealing millions from Australia's Chinese community
items.description: Justin thought he was being investigated by the Chinese police, but was pulled into a vicious and frightening scam targeting the Chinese diaspora all over the world.

items.title: Chalmers told tax changes threaten next wave of medical breakthroughs
items.description: Medical technology companies say new restrictions on tax refunds for research and development will hurt health startups in Australia.

items.title: Could a 'mansion tax' help the housing crisis?
items.description: Amid some of the most drastic proposed changes to Australia's tax system in decades and years of skyrocketing home values, one leading expert says it is an idea "worth considering".

items.title: Chris Minns has a no-frills plan to stop One Nation in NSW. Will it work?
items.description: NSW Premier Chris Minns is enjoying growing support in his electorate, but is still concerned about Pauline Hanson's presence in next year's state election.

items.title: Anthropic calls for AI freeze with fears humans risk 'losing control'
items.description: As a major AI company warns of an increased risk of "humans losing control over AI systems", the Trump administration says it will accelerate the development and use of artificial intelligence for national security applications.

items.title: Acid attack victim's lawyer describes trial of perpetrators as a 'sham'
items.description: Four military officers are facing trial over an acid attack on an Indonesian human rights campaigner that left him seriously disfigured. But some lawyers say the legal process is a "sham".

items.title: Andrew made money subletting cottages on his almost rent-free estate, watchdog finds
items.description: Former prince Andrew pocketed income from cottages on the Windsor estate while living at Royal Lodge under a lease that required virtually no rent, a watchdog report has found.

items.title: Anthony Head, known for roles in Buffy and Ted Lasso, dies
items.description: The British actor was well known for roles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso.

items.title: The 20-minute coffee van that keeps a small community together
items.description: Residents of the tiny town of Underbool, in Victoria's remote Mallee region, flock to this small coffee van, which has even smaller opening hours.

items.title: The club I wanted to join was waiting in Pompeii
items.description: A newly uncovered fresco in Pompeii tells the story of women, wine and Roman hedonism. Buried beneath the spectacle lies a lesson about restraint and why some discoveries should be left to the future.

items.title: How Matt Corby overcame 19 years of fear and found magic in tragedy
items.description: He got his start as a singing TV idol, but Matt Corby is making music for himself now, finding the magic in grief, growth and family.

items.title: 'Very troubled project': Hospital cost blowout concerns SA treasurer
items.description: The new Women's and Children's Hospital was priced at $3.2 billion in 2022, before inflation and other pressures sent costs in the construction industry soaring.

items.title: Putin says he sees 'no point' meeting Zelenskyy
items.description: A Ukrainian naval drone has exploded in Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta, as European leaders warned the war in Ukraine is becoming a "direct threat" to countries along the EU's eastern border.

items.title: Even kids want gambling ads banned, so why won't the government do it?
items.description: The government's proposed crackdown on gambling ads doesn't go as far as most Australians want. When you run the numbers, it's a win for the betting industry.

items.title: Residents say public housing works have blocked them from their own yards
items.description: Neighbours of a Homes Tasmania development in Burnie say excavation works have caused their land to start slipping downhill, restricting access to parts of their property.

items.title: Mental health royal commission update silent on hundreds of promised homes
items.description: A progress report on a major mental health inquiry sparks fears that a major housing commitment has fallen to the wayside.

items.title: Lorna has lived through two world wars, two pandemics and 26 Australian prime ministers
items.description: After a couple of years as the country's oldest woman, Lorna Henstridge is still going strong.

items.title: Fox ecstatic after winning first World Cup gold since surgery
items.description: Jessica Fox is beaming with pride, having recorded her first World Cup victory since returning to international competition after surgery to remove a benign tumour from her left kidney.

items.title: Piastri struggles in Monaco F1 practice as Ferrari makes statement
items.description: Oscar Piastri has failed to make an impression in the opening practice sessions at the Monaco Grand Prix.
